findings.kind: existing related conditional finding; selected current source witness
findings.trace: For an otherwise self-consistent tile, a 1-by-2 entry and local coordinate (1,0) flatten to index 1 and can return the (0,1) cell. The selected 95e assessment and reconstructed q120 already describe this first operation; this is not an executed package.
findings.historical_relationship: Reconstructed 059 q120 and f2c ledger 411 record the same first contract; preserve their own revision and null reader/path attribution. No new unique historical count or checkpoint 3821 recovery is asserted.
findings.connected_repair: Choose the outcome for an admitted selected entry whose local axis is outside its declared dimensions and prevent cross-row substitution. Preserve legitimate whole-chunk crop omission. Compare a post-decode per-axis error with broader ordinal/extent admission, including malformed fixture effects and error precedence; no option is selected.
findings.acceptance: Under the selected policy, an out-of-extent x or y cannot return a different cell. Higher-level behavior evidence should cover an in-extent neighbor, valid full/interior/true-edge geometry, omitted whole chunks, missing/outside cases, integrity and discriminant precedence, geographic edges and an affected consumer. These are proposed checks, not executed results.
findings.discovery: The row-alias first operation and emitted builder geometry are corroborated by source. External pack formats, partial coverage, exact geographic-boundary ownership, error/absence policy and aliases remain open.

findings.trace: Finite ordered bounds and a matching i16::MAX south tile can lead public cell lookup to evaluate south + 1 outside i16 range. Checked tactical origins and fixed transects differ from an API that accepts finite arbitrary offsets. Actual supported extreme input remains unproved.
findings.historical_relationship: Related by geographic bounds to f2c ledger 417, which instead traces the builder and i16::MIN tile-label arithmetic; equivalence is not established.
findings.connected_repair: Determine supported geographic contract and safe lookup arithmetic separately from chunk-axis checking.
findings.acceptance: Valid geographic edges retain intended mapping and invalid/extreme inputs do not overflow; exact policy remains open.
findings.discovery: bounded conditional source case; supported reach, policy and aliases remain open

findings.trace: A digest-consistent decoded canopy byte 101 passes the selected chunk checks; the builder instead maps source values above 100 to zero. Dispatcher conversion produces 10100 basis points and a later tactical grid validator rejects fields above 10000, if the selected path and prerequisites are reached.
findings.historical_relationship: Corrects v3's limited no-match search: reconstructed 059 q1668 asks the same percent-to-basis-point and regional admission question, with raw 255 -> 25500 as its own symbolic example. F2c ledger 280 reconnects the question to the separately identified 95e regional assessment, whose conditional finding 0 expressly uses the same 101 -> 10100 example as this source follow-up. No new historical unique count is added. Q1668 itself retains empty source/receipt arrays, zero body/population credit and no named reader or revision; do not insert the separate assessment's 6533 Segovb READ672 and role-2006 locator qualifications into that row. Earlier source credit does not transfer.
findings.connected_repair: Determine the authoritative byte contract and relevant ingestion and consumer semantics before selecting a change.
findings.acceptance: Admitted native cover and downstream units agree on the chosen bound, without weakening existing integrity checks.
findings.discovery: Bounded conditional source case; historical relationship corrected, but byte policy, real packages, supported producers, complete aliases and outcomes remain open.

findings.trace: With an otherwise admitted, digest-consistent manifest bounded approximately [-2e24, 0, 2e24, 1] and finite endpoints (0.5, -1e24) and (0.5, 1e24), the first expanded longitude window spans about 3e24. The ceil-to-usize conversion can saturate at usize::MAX, and the following +1 occurs before checked node-count multiplication. With overflow checks this can panic; behavior without them depends on the build. This is source reasoning, not a constructed package, executed route or observed incident.
findings.historical_relationship: Reconstructed 059 q603 broadly leaves terrain coordinate, window and bounds admission open; it does not identify this exact operation in its row. Its source and receipt arrays remain empty with zero population credit. This operation is distinct from cell south + 1 and f2c ledger 417 builder tile-label negation; complete historical alias review and supported extreme ingress remain open.
findings.connected_repair: Determine the supported geographic and route-window limits and size arithmetic contract separately from the chunk-axis decision.
findings.acceptance: For the chosen supported range, route-window dimension calculation cannot overflow before its bound check; ordinary valid routing retains its intended behavior.
findings.discovery: Conditional source question; reach, policy, aliases and disposition remain open

cross_lens_questions: Routing maps None to water and propagates Err; tactical required samples reject missing while optional peaks skip None but propagate errors. Regional capture retains holes. Strategic forage suppresses neighbor errors and absence but not center errors. Cultivation relief and road inference have separate error-erasure operations.

Reconstructed q128 and f2c ledger 441 concern relief-sample error handling; q130 and f2c ledger 442 concern road-plan omission. Ledger 441 also relates q283, whose recorded first operation is separate worker/CLI error formatting. Do not treat q128 and q283 as automatic aliases.
Cropped or undersized chunks, integral east/north boundary ownership, supported geographic limits, canopy byte policy and error precedence require decisions.
The surface enum and native byte decoder agree today; their independent numeric mappings are a future-change hazard, not a demonstrated current mismatch.
Coordinate, elevation and digest owner reuse requires separate policy, unit, wire and admission-timing review; it is not an observed wrong value by itself.
